8-amino substitution of purine analogues, such as 6-thioguanine and 2,2-difluorodeoxyadenosine, enhances PNP activity and diminishes their antitumor activity, whereas 8-amino-substituted 2,2'-difluorodeoxyguanosine retains antitumor activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 8-amino group in 3-deazapurines is detrimental to their antitumor activity, but it enhances their PNP inhibition.
the introduction of an amino group in the 8- or 2-position of 3-aza-7-deazaguanines enhances their inhibitory activities against PNP but diminishes or abolishes their antitumor activities.
the antitumor activity of 8-amidoguanines is not due to the inhibition of PNP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of 8-aminodeazaguanine is possible via the imidazole precursor 13, which is prepared from the monobicyclic rearrangement of dimethyldihydrooxadiazolylacrylate 10.
the 8-aminopurine moiety is not an essential structural feature of the antitumor activity of the 3-deaza analogue of guanine.
